subject: Temporary onboarding request: Bayshore CDN as provisional subprocessor
messages:
From: legal@bayshorecdn.com
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: j.smith@bayshorecdn.com
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Bayshore onboarding details & EU handling

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement/security review we need to confirm whether Bayshore (our CDN partner) can be listed as a temporary subprocessor for EU traffic to support the pilot next quarter. Specifically we need:

- A current subprocessor roster and the effective dates for any recent additions.
- A short data flow diagram showing whether payloads or logs transit via non-EU jurisdictions.
- Confirmation of encryption-in-transit and at-rest for the paths that touch Bayshore.
- Any provisional DPA amendment you can share (even a draft) and the expected turnaround for signature.

We have a short window; the customer expects the pilot to start 2029-04-15. If Bayshore can be onboarded provisionally for 30 days while we complete an attestation and DPA amendment, please confirm the conditions.

Attaching our onboarding checklist for your reference (attachment stub: bayshore_onboarding_checklist.pdf).

Best,
Joanna Smith
Contracts & Security
Bayshore Technologies
From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
To: legal@bayshorecdn.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Bayshore onboarding details & EU handling

Joanna —

Appreciate the clear list. We can support a provisional onboarding window with conditions listed below. I’m attaching our current subprocessor roster and a dataflow snapshot to get you started (attachment stubs included).

What we can offer immediately:
- Provisional access for up to 30 days starting on approval date to enable the pilot.
- Geo-fencing: we will route EU-origin requests to EU nodes; however some telemetry logs are replicated to an off-site analytics cluster (see dataflow diagram).
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; S3 AES-256 at rest for archives.
- We will prepare a DPA amendment draft and route for signature; expected internal review 3 business days, customer signature timeline dependent on you.

Conditions (must be agreed in writing):
1) No customer PII will be intentionally logged by Bayshore for the pilot; any logs that may contain user identifiers must be redacted before replication.
2) Temporary onboarding is conditional on a 30-day maximum and immediate deprovisioning if any evidence of exfiltration or misconfiguration is observed.
3) Bayshore must accept Redwood’s standard subprocessor addendum or sign the DPA amendment we’ll provide.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v4.csv; dataflow_diagram_v2.pdf

I’ve looped in Marissa (privacy lead) and Priyom (infrastructure) to confirm the operational details. If this is acceptable, I’ll send the provisional DPA amendment and a short attestation form for Bayshore to complete.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2029 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: Bayshore onboarding details & EU handling

Kim — quick clarifying Qs before we send the DPA draft:

- Can we make the provisional window explicit: start date = approval timestamp, end date = approval + 30 days? Marissa prefers a specific sunset clause.
- Priyom, is there any additional config required on the routing layer to ensure EU-only node enforcement, and can we log that change so we have an auditable flag?

I’m happy to add a short paragraph to the DPA amendment about sunset and audit logs. Also think we should require a read-only audit snapshot from Bayshore for the duration.

—Marissa
Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Bayshore onboarding details & EU handling

Marissa —

We can enforce EU node routing via an ACL on the edge-router group; it’s a config change and I can deploy it during a low-traffic window. We’ll emit an audit event when the ACL is enabled and add a routing-tag to requests that pass through Bayshore so you can trace any incident back to the config change.

I agree on requiring a read-only audit snapshot from Bayshore every 7 days for the provisional period. Also recommending we require a quick attestation form with these fields:
- Confirm no intentional PII logging for pilot (yes/no)
- Encryption cipher suites in use
- Contact for incident escalation (name, email, phone)

If you approve, Kimberly, I’ll schedule the ACL change and add the audit event to our control plane.

Thanks,
Priyom
Infra Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
To: legal@bayshorecdn.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Bayshore onboarding details & EU handling

Joanna —

Thanks for the patience. Confirming Redwood can provisionally onboard Bayshore for up to 30 days under the conditions below. We have attached the current roster and a dataflow snapshot; the provisional DPA amendment is attached as a draft for your review.

Provisional terms (summary):
- Window: approval timestamp -> approval + 30 days (explicit sunset clause included in draft).
- Routing: EU-origin traffic will be routed to EU Bayshore nodes. Priyom will enable an ACL and emit an audit event; we will tag requests that traverse Bayshore for traceability.
- Logging: No intentional capture of PII by Bayshore. Any telemetry or logs that may contain identifiers must be redacted. Weekly read-only audit snapshots from Bayshore are required.
- Security: TLS 1.2+ in transit; S3 AES-256 for any persisted artifacts.
- DPA: See attached provisional_dpa_amendment_bayshore.docx (draft). Please return a signed amendment or countersign within 10 business days.

Next steps:
1) Please complete the short attestation (fields described by Priyom) and return it to legal@redwoodinference.com within 3 business days.
2) We will schedule the ACL change on our edge during a low-traffic window and will notify you 24 hours in advance.
3) Once we receive the attestation and countersigned DPA, we will lift the provisional sunset constraint and move to normal onboarding.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v4.csv; dataflow_diagram_v2.pdf; provisional_dpa_amendment_bayshore.docx

Regards,

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
